what: Bags or cubic yards for slabs, footings and post holes
title: Concrete Calculator: How Many Bags of Concrete Do I Need? | Calcupine
description: Calculate bags or cubic yards of concrete for slabs, footings, post holes, round and square columns, steps and curbs, with waste included. Feet, inches or metric.
lede: Choose a slab, footing, post holes, columns, steps or a curb, enter the size, and get the number of bags or cubic yards to order. The example is a 10 by 10 foot patio, 4 inches thick.

faq.q: How many 80 lb bags of concrete make a yard?
faq.a: One cubic yard is 27 cubic feet, and an 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 cubic feet, so it takes 45 bags. With 60 lb bags (0.45 cu ft) it takes 60, and with 40 lb bags (0.30 cu ft) it takes 90.

faq.q: How many bags for a 10x10 slab 4 inches thick?
faq.a: A 10 by 10 foot slab at 4 inches is 33.3 cubic feet. With 10% extra that is 36.7 cubic feet, or 62 bags of 80 lb mix. At about 1.4 cubic yards, ready-mix delivery is usually the easier choice.

faq.q: When should I order ready-mix instead of bags?
faq.a: Around 1 cubic yard (45 bags of 80 lb mix) is where most people switch. Mixing that many bags by hand is slow, and the first part of a slab can start setting before you finish. Some suppliers charge a short-load fee for small orders, so ask.

faq.q: How thick should a concrete slab be?
faq.a: 4 inches is typical for patios, walkways and shed floors. Driveways and areas that carry vehicles are usually 5 to 6 inches. Local codes and soil conditions can require more, so check with your building department.

faq.q: How much extra concrete should I buy?
faq.a: Plan for 5 to 10% extra. Ground is rarely perfectly flat, forms bow a little, and running short mid-pour leaves a weak joint. The calculator adds 10% unless you change it.

faq.q: How much concrete do I need for steps?
faq.a: Pick Steps, then enter the number of steps, the rise and run of each one, the width and the depth of the top step or landing. The calculator stacks the steps as solid blocks, so 3 steps that are 4 ft wide, 7 in high and 11 in deep take about 12.8 cu ft before waste, or about 24 bags of 80 lb mix with 10% extra.

faq.q: How do I work out concrete for a curb and gutter?
faq.a: Multiply the length by the curb's cross-section (width x height) and add the gutter pan (width x thickness). A 50 ft run of 6 x 18 in curb with a 24 x 6 in gutter is 87.5 cu ft, or about 3.2 cubic yards before waste.
